why: Case verdicts whose classification is already known. The suite record holds rates and step verdicts but no cap fractions or broker counters, so a change to what makes a case valid cannot be replayed against it. These can. A case is either a scaling claim (the component under test was the constraint), a ceiling observation (something else was, which is a finding and not a defect), or invalid (the measurement itself cannot be trusted). Rates were not recorded here, because no rule needed them -- which means a rule that asks 'was this suspected ceiling actually slower than its siblings?' cannot be replayed at all. Clean-room run 42's cases carry rates so that it can be.
